extracted.intended_audience: scholarly communication researchers, journal editors, and open science practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Systematic review that defines and maps distinct traits of Open Peer Review (OPR) to clarify usage and enable focused analysis of OPR models; intended to guide researchers, editors and platform designers. Includes supplementary materials (PRISMA) and data for reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPR definition (umbrella term)
rubrics_metrics.description: Open peer review is an umbrella term for a number of overlapping ways that peer review models can be adapted in line with the aims of Open Science, including making reviewer and author identities open, publishing review reports and enabling greater participation in the peer review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author argues that OPR is ambiguous and should be treated as an umbrella concept composed of distinct traits; disambiguating these traits enables clearer discussion and focused empirical analysis of their effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open identities
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors and reviewers are aware of each other’s identity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Making identities open is one trait of OPR; implications for bias, reviewer behaviour and accountability should be considered when applying this trait.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Review reports are published alongside the relevant article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishing review reports increases transparency of the review process; evaluation should consider effects on review quality, reproducibility and community trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open participation
rubrics_metrics.description: The wider community to able to contribute to the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Openness of participation can vary by discipline (noted differences between SSH and STEM); assessors should consider how broader participation affects expertise, noise, and inclusivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open interaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct reciprocal discussion between author(s) and reviewers, and/or between reviewers, is allowed and encouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitates dialogue and potential mentorship; reviewers and editors should consider moderation, civility norms, and the impact on review thoroughness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open pre-review manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts are made immediately available (e.g., via pre-print servers like arXiv) in advance of any formal peer review procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-printing decouples dissemination from formal review and can enable early community feedback; consider effects on priority, versioning, and downstream citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open final-version commenting
rubrics_metrics.description: Review or commenting on final “version of record” publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables post-publication critique on the authoritative version; consider how editorial policies, indexing, and corrections/retractions are handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open platforms ("decoupled review")
rubrics_metrics.description: Review is facilitated by a different organizational entity than the venue of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also described as “decoupled review”; the text and reviewers note this as an unusual or 'fringe' case of OPR, and caution that peer review as a process can be distinct from its technological implementation (avoid techno-determinism).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer status definitions (F1000Research)
rubrics_metrics.description: Approved; Approved with reservations; Not approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions provided: 'Approved' = scientifically sound in its current form with only minor improvements suggested; 'Approved with reservations' = a number of small changes, sometimes more significant revisions required; 'Not approved' = fundamental flaws seriously undermine findings and conclusions. These statuses form the decision rubric used by the journal's peer review system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Are the rationale for, and objectives of, the Systematic Review clearly stated?
rubrics_metrics.description: Review-question/form item used by F1000Research reviewers to assess whether the paper's aims and rationale are clearly presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit evaluation item in reviewer reports; typical answers include Yes/Partly/No with accompanying comments explaining clarity and framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Are sufficient details of the methods and analysis provided to allow replication by others?
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer assessment item asking whether methods and analysis are described in enough detail to permit reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers may mark Partly/Yes/No and request inclusion of search terms, databases searched, selection criteria and limitations; the paper's reviewers asked for more detail on searching social sciences and humanities literature and for methods limitations to be outlined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the statistical analysis and its interpretation appropriate?
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer assessment item addressing whether statistical methods and their interpretation are correct and suitable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers may defer judgment if not qualified (e.g., 'I cannot comment. A qualified statistician is required'); authors should provide sufficient statistical detail or consult statisticians when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Are the conclusions drawn adequately supported by the results presented in the review?
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer item assessing whether conclusions are supported by the presented evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical responses include Yes/Partly/No; reviewers asked for stronger methodological framing when conclusions rely on contested definitions (e.g., 'open science').

rubrics_metrics.name: Data availability / Dataset DOI
rubrics_metrics.description: Dataset including full data files used for analysis in this review: http://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.438024
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper provides a DOI-linked dataset for transparency and to enable replication/reuse; reviewers and readers are expected to be able to access and inspect supporting data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary materials: PRISMA checklist and flowchart
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary file 1: PRISMA checklist. Supplementary file 2: PRISMA flowchart showing the number of records identified, included and excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of PRISMA materials is a methodological standard for systematic reviews to document search and selection processes; the checklist was completed with the original copy of the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: This work is funded by the European Commission H2020 project OpenAIRE2020 (Grant agreement: 643410, Call: H2020-EINFRA-2014-1). The funders had no role in study design, data collection and analysis, decision to publish, or preparation of the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit funding statements should disclose grant identifiers and describe funder involvement (or lack thereof) in the research process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing interests declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Competing interests: This work was conducted as part of the OpenAIRE2020 project, an EC-funded initiative to implement and monitor Open Access and Open Science policies in Europe and beyond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must disclose competing interests; reviewers also declare competing interests in their reports (e.g., 'No competing interests were disclosed' or noting employment that may be relevant).

rubrics_metrics.name: Author contributions (CRediT-style roles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Author roles listed: Conceptualization, Data Curation, Formal Analysis, Investigation, Methodology, Project Administration, Resources, Software, Supervision, Validation, Visualization, Writing – Original Draft Preparation, Writing – Review & Editing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed attribution of contributions (CRediT taxonomy) is used to clarify author responsibilities and credit; include such statements for transparency and accountability.
